comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
Glad you got it to work by installing [`python-certifi-win32`](https://pypi.org/project/python-certifi-win32/)! Presumably installing [`pip-system-certs`](https://pypi.org/project/pip-system-certs/) would have also worked since it is a replacement for `python-certifi-win32`.

https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/4909 has some additional context too.

What are the contents of your `packages.yml` file? I'm curious which of the five (5) different methods you were trying to use:
1. [Hub packages](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/packages#hub-packages-recommended)
1. [Git packages](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/packages#git-packages)
1. [Internally hosted tarball URL](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/packages#internally-hosted-tarball-url)
1. [Private packages](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/packages#private-packages)
1. [Local packages](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/packages#local-packages)

Also, did you try running this for a Python version other than 3.11? I'm wondering if this worked without modification in Python <= 3.10 and then stopped working in 3.11.

The last thing I'm wondering about is if this would have affected you with a different operating system like a Linux distribution or macOS or if it only affected Windows?

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
@moseleyi two questions for you:
1. Which operating system are you using when you get this error?
2. Are you using a corporate VPN, by any chance?

### Windows operating system

Windows users have been able to resolve this with [these](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/8554#issuecomment-1708250636) instructions:

```shell
python -m pip install python-certifi-win32
```

### Corporate VPN

[At least one](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/7427#issuecomment-1520194576) corporate VPN user was able to resolve this by setting the [`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/advanced/#ssl-cert-verification) environment variable.

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
Hi @vidhyaguru, this looks like an issue in your local environment rather than a bug in dbt-core. It's just a matter of figuring out what the missing piece is within your local environment.

[Here](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/8554#issuecomment-1715874918) is a write-up that includes a high-level explanation as well as as variety of approaches that have worked for others. In particular, it has a sample Python script for troubleshooting. Using this script removes `dbt` from the equation and allows you to focus on your local environment.

Let us know how it goes!

comments.author: dbeatty10
comments.body:
> getting timeout when run from a baremetal host with vpn.

@vidhyaguru My suggestion for next steps would be to add the Python script explained [here](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/8554#issuecomment-1715874918) to your baremetal host.

[At least one](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/7427#issuecomment-1520194576) corporate VPN user was able to resolve their networking issues by setting the [`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user/advanced/#ssl-cert-verification) environment variable.

The write-up [here](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/8554#issuecomment-1715874918) really the best and most detailed troubleshooting options we know about. It should give you good launching off points for further research on your own.
